items.description: The Australian government is under pressure to explain why it allowed dozens of Israeli soldiers into the country.

items.title: Guinea-Bissau votes to reshape presidency
items.description: The West African nation's military government wants to amend the constitution to give more powers to the president. The junta, which seized power last year, says it will hold elections in December.

items.title: Niger junta says it is back in control after attempted coup
items.description: Niamey airport and the presidential palace were targeted on Saturday, as well as the national television station, which went off the air for just over an hour.

items.title: Srebrenica survivor Ahmed Hrustanovic reflects on Ratko Mladic's death
items.description: Ahmed Hrustanovic reflects on Ratko Mladic's death with NPR's Scott Simon. All of Hrustanovic's adult male relatives died in the Srebrenica Massacre engineered by Mladic.

items.title: 'Only The Truth Matters': Families Of Srebrenica, Sarajevo Victims React To Mladic's Death
items.description: Families who lost loved ones in the 1995 Srebrenica massacre and in the siege of Sarajevo say the death of former Bosnian Serb military commander Ratko Mladic on August 27 does little to ease decades of grief. But one man says what matters most is that Mladic was held accountable for his crimes, which included genocide…

items.title: Four children killed as separate attacks in Gaza destroy aid supplies
items.description: Israeli attacks killed four children and destroyed humanitarian aid supplies in what turned out to be a deadly week in war-ravaged Gaza, the UN emergency relief agency, OCHA, said on Friday.
